Apple has updated the Apple Store app's privacy policy to include terms related to its upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details are as follows.

Apple is expanding its use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

According to MacRumors, a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant" has been added to the Apple Store app and its privacy page, with the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon introduce a chatbot feature that provides personalised responses based on user data and helps users make purchasing decisions.

Apple states that before sharing conversation content with an unnamed partner to generate assistant responses, it will first remove personally identifiable information, suggesting that at least part of the experience is likely powered by a third-party company's model.

Chat records will be retained within the app for users to review, while also being stored by Apple for business analytics purposes. Users can choose whether to allow their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant through a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

Judging from the wording in Apple's privacy policy, the virtual assistant may initially launch only in select countries and regions, most likely debuting in English-speaking markets before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This announcement comes months after Apple added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app, which provides sales and technical support resources for Apple retail partners. Staff can access the chatbot through the "Ask" tab, where the system answers questions based on official Apple training materials and documentation.

Additionally, Bloomberg earlier reported that Apple has been testing a system called "Live Notes" at some retail stores, which uses artificial intelligence to record, transcribe, and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing staff to focus on customers without being distracted by note-taking.
